title: The Unexpected Bakery
premise: Marine biologist Orsen Dunmore inherits half of a crumbling orchard bakery from the grandmother he barely knew — and discovers the other half belongs to Wren Ashby, the childhood friend he abandoned twelve years ago. Forced to co-run the bakery through one harvest festival season to satisfy the deed's stubborn terms, they rebuild more than sourdough starters and stone walls. When a prestigious research post in the Azores demands Orsen leave before the festival, he must choose between the career that once saved him from grief and the found family of bakers, orchard hands, and neighbors who finally make him belong. He stays through the festival's final night, signs the deed over fully to Wren while taking a partnership in the business instead of a lab title, and chooses love with better timing at last.
about_author: L. M. Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former pastry chef turned novelist who writes small-town romances about second chances and stubborn inheritances. They live in an old farmhouse with a temperamental wood stove and a sourdough starter older than their career.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. On a research vessel off the Azores, Orsen counts nesting turtles and dodges his sister's calls about a letter from a lawyer. He learns his estranged grandmother has died and left him something in Willow Creek. Emotional beat: guarded grief for a woman he never let himself mourn.

chapters.title: The Deed That Argues Back
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. In Willow Creek, lawyer Pru Halloway reveals the deed: Orsen co-owns Dunmore's Orchard Bakery with one Wren Ashby, and the will requires both heirs to run it together through harvest festival or lose it entirely. Emotional beat: dread curdling into curiosity.

chapters.title: Flour on His Hands
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, who spent years earning her place in Grandma Ida's kitchen after her own family fell apart, learns the co-heir is Orsen — the boy who left without goodbye. She decides to make him so miserable he sells. Emotional beat: righteous anger masking old hurt.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The two meet over Ida's will and negotiate ground rules like hostile nations signing a treaty: split shifts, separate counters, no personal questions. Emotional beat: brittle professionalism stretched over twelve years of silence.

chapters.title: The Starter Named After Nobody
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A power outage threatens Ida's hundred-year-old sourdough starter; Orsen shows up unasked and keeps the ovens' pilot flames lit all night. Wren finds him asleep flour-dusted at dawn. Emotional beat: the first crack in her armor.

chapters.title: Regulars
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The bakery's morning regulars — retired ferry captain Dot, teen apprentice Milo, beekeeper Sam — adopt Orsen with terrifying warmth, filling gaps he didn't know he had. He starts staying past his shift. Emotional beat: belonging sneaking up on him.

chapters.title: Ida's Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. While cataloguing recipes for the festival menu, Wren and Orsen find cards in Ida's handwriting addressed to both of them — lessons she wrote knowing they'd return together someday. Emotional beat: realizing Ida engineered this reunion deliberately.

chapters.title: The Azores Offer
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. His dream research fellowship lands: lead marine biologist, two-year post, departure date six weeks before the festival ends. He hides the letter in his duffel. Emotional beat: guilt arriving ahead of ambition.

chapters.title: Apple Thieves
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Chasing raccoons out of the orchard at midnight, the two get caught in rain under the oldest apple tree, laughing for the first time since childhood. Almost-kiss interrupted by Milo's flashlight. Emotional beat: tension turning tender.

chapters.title: What Orsen Ran From
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Milo's innocent questions push Wren to learn why Orsen vanished at nineteen: his father's death, a mother who left, a scholarship he took to survive. Her anger softens into something more dangerous. Emotional beat: compassion complicating everything.

chapters.title: The Festival Committee
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The town drafts them to co-chair the Harvest Festival, forcing public collaboration — planning meetings, shared spreadsheets, arguments about pie contests that dissolve into laughter. Emotional beat: partnership feeling dangerously natural.

chapters.title: First Kiss, Burnt Batch
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Testing festival pastries at 2 a.m., flour-fight turns into their first kiss. The batch burns; neither cares until morning panic sets in. Emotional beat: joy immediately shadowed by fear of repeating history.

chapters.title: Timing
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Wren finds the hidden fellowship letter. She doesn't rage — she tells him to take it, which hurts worse than any fight. Emotional beat: the old wound reopening exactly as predicted.

chapters.title: Cold Counter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They retreat into polite strangers again: clipped orders, separate shifts, the regulars noticing and grieving quietly. Dot confronts Orsen: 'Your grandmother didn't leave you a bakery. She left you a chance.' Emotional beat: loneliness inside the same room.

chapters.title: Milo Runs Away (Briefly)
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Milo, whose foster placement is fraying, disappears overnight; Orsen finds him sleeping in the orchard treehouse and brings him home without calling anyone first. Emotional beat: Orsen choosing this family instinctively, before he can talk himself out of it.

chapters.title: The Treehouse Conversation
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen admits to Wren that the ocean was never the dream — it was the escape hatch. The fellowship would save his career but cost the first life that ever felt like his. Emotional beat: honesty offered without asking for anything back.

chapters.title: Festival Eve
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Final preparations consume everyone; Wren and Orsen work in wordless sync, and she realizes she doesn't want the bakery without him in it — but won't ask him to stay and become his reason for resentment. Emotional beat: love choosing not to hold on too tight.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. On festival morning, Orsen stands at the dock with his packed bag as the fellowship coordinator calls. He watches the bakery lights across the water, the crowd gathering, Wren's silhouette in the window. Emotional beat: the decision hanging in salt air.

chapters.title: Cider and Confessions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Orsen arrives mid-festival, declines the call publicly, and confesses before the whole town: he's been running his whole life, and Willow Creek is the first place he wants to stand still. Wren, furious and moved, makes him say it to her alone. Emotional beat: public declaration, private reckoning.

chapters.title: The Deed, Rewritten
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At Pru's office Monday, Orsen restructures his inheritance: not selling, but converting his half into a minority partnership funding a marine-education program attached to the bakery, keeping his science alive on his own terms. Emotional beat: refusing the false choice between career and love.

chapters.title: What the Orchard Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Under the oldest apple tree, they plant a sapling from Ida's grafts and read her recipe-card letters aloud together. Milo asks, tentatively, if he could maybe stay on permanently. Emotional beat: found family formalizing itself gently.

chapters.title: Opening Day, Again
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Spring reopening: new sign reading 'Dunmore & Ashby,' turtles postcards from Orsen's remote research partners, Wren pulling the first loaves. Orsen finally answers what timing means to him now. Emotional beat: quiet, earned happiness — second chances kept.
